115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, challenging the order dated 25.09.2025 passed in E.P.N

o. 
654 of 2021 in A.O.P. No. 226 of 2018 on the file of the VII Additional District Judge, Vijayawada.

2. Heard Sri Akhil Krishnan, learned counsel representing Sri S.S.Varma, learned Standing Counsel for the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), appearing for the petitioner.
3.
For the order proposed to be passed and as keeping the petition pending to issue notice to the respondent, would serve no useful purpose.

Notice to the respondent is dispensed with, but his interest would be safeguarded.
4.

An arbitral Award dated 29.06.2019 was passed by the Arbitrator & Joint Collector-II, Krishna District, in favour of the 1st respondent herein and against the revision petitioner, enhancing the compensation in respect of the acquisition of certain extent of land for widening of NH-16.
5.

Aggrieved from the Award dated 29.06.2019, the petitioner filed A.O.P. No. 226 of 2018 on the file of the XI Additional District Judge, Gudivada, along with an application seeking stay of execution of the Award.

(RNT,J & MRK,J C.R.P.NO.2863 OF 2025 )
6.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the stay application filed along with the petition under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 is still pending consideration.
He submits that though the delay in filing the petition was condoned, the application for interim relief has not been disposed of till date.

sentences.text: He further submits that, in the meantime, the 1st respondent filed E.P.No. 654 of 2021 for execution of the Award, and in the said E.P., the impugned order dated 25.09.2025 has been passed.
He submits that the Executing Court has taken the view that unless stay is granted, the execution proceedings can be continued.

7. The grievance raised is that, on the one hand the application seeking stay of the Award is pending consideration since 2021, which remains undisposed of, and on the other hand, the Award is being put to execution.

8. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner, we are of the considered view that, in terms of Section 36(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an Award becomes executable unless stayed by an order of the Court.

However, once an application seeking grant of stay of the Award is filed, the same is required to be considered and disposed of expeditiously, so as to balance the rights of both parties and to avoid rendering the proceedings under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 infructuous.

(RNT,J & MRK,J C.R.P.NO.2863 OF 2025 )
9.

Accordingly, this Civil Revision Petition is disposed of, with a direction to the XI Additional District Judge, Gudivada, to consider the application seeking stay of the Award dated 29.06.2019,
and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, after giving due opportunity of hearing to the 1st respondent herein, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of four (04) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

10. Till disposal of the stay application, the further execution proceedings pursuant to the impugned Award and the impugned order dated 25.09.2025 shall remain stayed, subject to the condition that the petitioner deposits 1/3rd of the amount under execution, before the Executing Court within a period of two (02) weeks from today.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall also stand closed.

RAVI NATH TILHARI, J ______________________________ MAHESWARA RAO KUNCHEAM, J Date : 05.11.2025.
RPD.
